problem.p: Business documents (invoices, delivery notes, quotes, labels) and diagrams currently go through HTML-to-PDF conversion or ReportLab in genro-print.
Typst is a typesetting engine written in Rust and licensed under Apache-2.0. It compiles text source to PDF, SVG and PNG.
This project describes documents with a genro-builders grammar and delegates typesetting to Typst.

The eventual goal is a Gramlot letterhead editor similar to GenroPy's, and a print editor for business applications: lists, pages and forms. Editors are outside this project. genro-typst supplies the grammar, persistence format and renderer.

current.fact: genro-print separates the grammar (builders with document, platypus, canvas, lrc, styled and charts mixins) from ReportLab renderers. Each builder exposes its renderer through the property renderer_reportlab and _default_render_mode = "reportlab".
In genro-print the move from compilers/ to renderers/ is in the working tree, uncommitted. The latest commit is dated 2026-04-07.

The genro-builders SVG dialect has three parts: SvgBuilder (grammar, _name = "svg"), SvgElements (elements declared with @element), SvgRenderer (subclass of RendererBase, mode = "svg", method rendered_item) exposed by the property renderer_svg.

section.title: Principle
section.rule: The grammar describes business documents, not the Typst language. It does not wrap the entire Typst language.
The renderer emits fixed Typst constructs. Builder users never write Typst code.
section.p: The model follows GenroPy's Layout/Row/Cell: a feature inventory with one abstract object per feature. For example, "page X of Y" is a dedicated element whose renderer emits a snippet of context.

row.cell: repeated footer verified; page carryover unverified
SVG from the genro-builders svg dialect, included with image

section.title: Prototype grammar
section.p: Based on GenroPy's Layout/Row/Cell (gnr/core/gnrhtml.py). In the legacy system each element has an absolute position in um (millimeters), and width=0/height=0 divides free space equally. Here layout follows the flow and can continue on the next page.

list.item: A row without height takes the height of its content (auto). '1fr' is allowed only if the layout has a height.
A width is a length, percentage or fraction: '25mm', '30%', '2fr', 'auto'. A number is a fraction; width=0 means 1fr, as in the legacy system.
Removed: um and lbl_height. top/left/bottom/right become inset.

row.cell: name, font, size, weight, color, align
border_width, border_color, border_style, row_border, cell_border, lbl_class, content_class, inset
height, row_border, cell_border, lbl_class, content_class, breakable
content, width, lbl, lbl_class, content_class, cell_border, align, valign, background, colspan
src (including an SvgBuilder), width, height, fit
field, name, width, dtype, format, align, totalize, subtotal, background, color
column of table; totalize produces table.footer

section.p: A cell can contain a nested layout. colspan does not exist in the legacy system. Attributes of column come from the legacy grid structure (gnr/web/gnrbaseclasses.py); mm_width becomes width.
Legacy names are retained: lbl, lbl_class, content_class, border_width, row_border, cell_border, totalize. New names use camelCase.

list.item: Everything is data. Letterheads and print documents are Bags serialized with TYTX. Every grammar attribute is a value an editor can set. No element requires Python code (the legacy system required calcRowHeight and prepareRow).
Formatted text. The legacy system stored HTML from ckEditor for each region. The prototype grammar does not yet have inline elements for bold, italic or a field within a sentence.
Data fields. The legacy system used $campo in HTML, filled by templateReplace. Here the pointers are ^ from genro-builders; the editor offers fields from the table model.
Preprinted forms. Lists and pages use elastic layout. A preprinted form has fields at fixed positions in millimeters, requiring an absolute-position element (place with dx/dy in Typst).
Browser preview. The Bag-to-Typst renderer is in Python. The browser compiles Typst code with typst.ts.

row.cell: LRC in mm over a preprinted form

section.title: How GenroPy works
section.fact: A letterhead is a record in adm.htmltemplate. The column data is a Bag: main.page.{height,width,top,left,right,bottom} in mm, main.design (headline or sidebar), with a size and HTML containing variables for each region: $campo. Document content goes into the region center_center.

based_on links a letterhead to its parent; letterheadChain builds the chain, with each letterhead becoming an overlay. next_letterhead identifies the letterhead for pages after the first (gnr/core/gnrhtml.py, newPage).
The legacy editor has a form with page dimensions, a tab for design, a preview with resizable regions, and ckEditor for the selected region's HTML.

section.title: Proposal
section.code: letterhead(name='invoice', paper='a4', flipped=False, margin_top='30mm', margin_bottom='20mm', margin_left='35mm', margin_right='15mm', basedOn='base') region(name='top', pages='first', size='30mm') # LRC content with ^ pointers region(name='top', pages='others', size='15mm') region(name='left', size='25mm') region(name='background') document(letterhead='invoice')

list.item: top → header; bottom → footer; left, right, background → background with place; watermark → foreground.
pages='first'|'others' replaces next_letterhead: context on counter(page).
basedOn replaces based_on: regions with the same name and pages replace those in the base; regions named background accumulate.
main.design is removed: headline and sidebar are choices of regions.
The letterhead is a Bag serialized with TYTX (Bag.to_tytx, Bag.from_tytx). The document loads it and grafts it into its source.

section.fact: Typst 0.15.0: different first and subsequent page headers using context, sidebar using background + place. Both appear in a two-page PDF.
Typst does not enlarge the top margin for a taller header: a 40 mm header with a 10 mm margin overlaps the body. Each region's margin must be declared as a length.
section.p: A builder Bag must reload from TYTX with its tags and pass grammar validation. This is unverified.

section.title: Existing Typst editors
section.fact: typst.ts compiles Typst in the browser through WASM. Apache-2.0 license, release v0.7.0 dated 2026-06-01.

Open-source visual Typst editors are young: TyX (MIT), typster (MIT), ortic/typst-wysiwyg (MIT, prototype). TyX works on TipTap JSON and compiles it into Typst code, following the same pattern as this project.
section.p: The renderer produces actual Typst code. The path is one-way: edits to Typst code do not flow back into the Bag.

list.item: Text escaping: # * _ $ @ < and other markup characters.
Converting Python types to Typst types: lengths (2cm, 1fr, 50%), colors, none/auto, alignment, identifiers distinct from strings.

section.title: Verified Python binding
section.fact: The PyPI package typst 0.15.0 bundles Typst 0.15.0 (sys.version in the document prints 0.15.0).

Public API: compile, compile_with_warnings, query, eval, Compiler, Fonts, FontInfo, TypstError, TypstWarning. compile accepts source as bytes, a path or a string; formats pdf, svg, png, html; parameters sys_inputs, pdf_standards (including PDF/A), timestamp, root. Compiler accepts font_paths, ignore_system_fonts, package_path, package_cache_path.
A three-page document with a 120-row table compiles without files: typst.compile(bytes, format="pdf"). First call: 0.62 s; with an existing Compiler: 0.014 s.

rule.why: Typst is pre-1.0; syntax changes between minor versions.

section.rule: The binding version is pinned with == in pyproject.toml.

section.title: Browser preview
section.p: typst.ts (WASM) compiles the same source in the browser. This is unverified.

decision.question: Should page totals (carried forward / brought forward) use context code generated by the renderer, or Python calculations before typesetting?
Should the grammar reuse genro-print names (layout, row, cell, paragraph, table) or define its own?
Should external Typst packages (e.g. tiaoma) download on first compilation or ship with the project through package_path?
Should we use system fonts or ship a font directory with the project (ignore_system_fonts=True) for identical PDFs on every server?
Should formatted text in regions and cells use inline grammar elements, or should the renderer convert the format of the text editor chosen for Gramlot?
Should the Gramlot preview request Typst code from the server, or should the renderer be ported to genro-builders-js to run entirely in the browser?

consequences.p: Printing no longer depends on ReportLab or a headless browser. It depends on a pinned pre-1.0 Rust library.
